system: You are a careful research assistant.
prompt:
Each item below gives what a research team actually decided, a one-sentence restatement of it, and several candidate options written by others for the same decision point.

For each item answer:
- "faithful": "yes" if the restatement describes the same decision as what the team decided (abstracting away study-specific details is fine), "no" if it changes, drops the core of, or adds to the decision.
- "same": for each candidate label, "same" if the candidate is essentially the team's decision (a reader who knew what the team did would say the team took this option, or it contains the team's decision as a part), else "different".

Return only JSON: {"items": [{"key": str, "faithful": "yes" | "no", "same": {"<label>": "same" | "different"}}]}

ITEMS:

=== key a42c26006934
What the team decided: Used multiple independent models (recorded speech, internet users, popular platforms, CommonCrawl, indexed websites) and aggregated them rather than relying on a single estimate
Restatement: Estimate the data stock with several independent models, each grounded in a different source, and aggregate their results instead of trusting a single estimate.
C1: Build separate upper and lower stock bounds for each domain, count only sources the team can size credibly, and document every excluded source with reasons.
C2: Produce one central stock estimate per domain by summing the largest measurable sources and treating the long tail of smaller sources as a minor correction.

=== key 547e35b877ba
What the team decided: Focused on the stock and accumulation rates of unlabeled data
Restatement: Restrict the stock estimate to unlabeled data alone, tracking its stock and accumulation rate while leaving the much smaller labeled supply outside the accounting.
C1: Count unlabeled and labeled data as separate categories, report the stock for each independently, and present any combined figure only as a secondary summary.
C2: Count all usable text and imagery toward a single stock figure, folding labeled data into the unlabeled total since generated pseudo-labels blur the distinction.

=== key 9f25dada467a
What the team decided: Defined high-quality data by deferring to practitioners' choices, i.e. the composition of datasets used to train large LMs, and by the presence of a usefulness/quality filter
Restatement: Defer to practitioners' choices: count language data as high quality when it appears in datasets used to train large models or has passed a usefulness filter.
C1: Restrict high quality to curated source types such as books and papers, and report the resulting stock under several alternative inclusion cutoffs as a check.
C2: Treat curated sources like books and scientific papers as the high-quality stock and count every other public text source toward the low-quality stock figure.

=== key af43df6fa8f3
What the team decided: Interpreted the high end of the range as coming from highly theoretical models they trust least, and gave practical readings of 1e14, 1e15 and 1e16 words
Restatement: Treat the top of the range as coming from the least trusted theoretical models and present practical readings at round values spanning the three orders of magnitude.
C1: Report the full three-order-of-magnitude range as the estimate, carry both endpoints through the projections, and show exhaustion timing for each extreme case.
C2: Take the geometric midpoint of the range as the working stock estimate, note the wide uncertainty in one line, and carry the single figure into the projections.

=== key 56755b305a8f

Restatement: State that the method is only useful when speed is essential and that other approaches are probably better in most other circumstances.
C1: Describe the method as useful for fast approximate uncertainty estimation and enumerate each failure mode and assumption separately, marking every claimed capability with the evidence supporting it.
C2: Describe the method as a practical fast uncertainty estimator and note briefly that it is approximate, without cataloging every case where the approximation could degrade.
